subject: Recap: Echelon Health discovery — pilot goals, decision lane & next steps
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sara Wells <sara.wells@echelonhealth.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@echelonhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: Echelon Health discovery — pilot goals, decision lane & next steps

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for taking time today. Thought it would be helpful to capture what we heard, proposed next steps, and an initial mutual plan so your team can share with procurement and legal. Please confirm or correct anything below.

Key pain points you described
- High latency and unpredictable cost for nightly clinical note summarization jobs (current infra spikes during batch windows).
- Loss of model performance when you downscale GPUs; engineering overhead to maintain multiple model variants.
- Need for strict PHI controls and audit logs (SOC2 + customer-managed keys).

Primary goals for a 6–8 week pilot
1) Reduce per-record inference cost by 30% on average for nightly batch runs.
2) Keep 99th-percentile latency under 250ms for interactive QA flows.
3) Validate VPC-deployed private runtime with KMS integration and audit logging that satisfies your compliance team.

Success metrics (how we’ll measure)
- Cost: tokens per run and $/1k-records compared to current baseline.
- Latency: p50/p90/p99 for the interactive endpoint.
- Security: KMS key rotation test + audit log export to your S3.

Proposed pilot scope (what Redwood will deliver)
- Dedicated pilot cluster (private mode) accessible from your VPC, model onboarding of one LLM variant, and a sample batching config optimized for nightly runs.
- Endpoint for interactive QA with a traffic mirroring option for validation.
- Weekly syncs + a short eval report at pilot midpoint and close.

Stakeholders we captured
- Echelon: Sara Wells (Product / Pilot owner), Tom Alvarez (Infrastructure / Procurement), Priya Menon (Security — TBD in procurement thread).
- Redwood: Mina Haddad (AE / owner), Ben Carter (Solutions), Lauren Bishop (Customer Success / pilot ops).

Decision process & timeline you described
- Procurement review window: 2–3 calendar weeks starting once we provide a draft MPA and security artifacts.
- Legal signoff: target by Nov 30.
- Exec approval: informal CTO nod by week of Nov 22.

Immediate asks from you
1) Confirm the three pilot success metrics above and add any absolute targets you want us to bake into the evaluation.
2) Confirm the names/emails of anyone who should get the security questionnaire from our team (we’ll send the XLS).
3) Confirm availability for an MPA review on Nov 18 (30–45m).

Attached: redwood-mpa-draft-20261113.pdf (initial mutual plan draft)
We also have the security questionnaire ready — I’ll attach an Excel for your security team to complete if that’s helpful.

If that looks right I’ll update the MPA with the explicit timelines and circulate a DocuSign link for the procurement lane so your legal team has a clean artifact to review.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com | (415) 555-0134

- Security: Priya Menon is the right contact; she’s out next week but if we can get the questionnaire over now she’ll have bandwidth the week after Thanksgiving. Please send the XLS to priya.menon@echelonhealth.com and cc procurement.
- Procurement timeline: our procurement team is tied up until Nov 23; expect an official 2-week review after that, so Nov 24–Dec 8 is realistic for procurement review.
- Exec approval: I can get an informal go/no-go from CTO by Nov 19 but formal exec signoff will follow procurement/legal.

A couple of edits to pilot goals: please add data retention verification (ability to set TTLs and verify deletion) as a success metric.

I’ve attached the security questions that our team typically completes when evaluating vendors — it’ll speed up legal once you return a completed copy.

Sara
